note: Eval set in the agentskills.io evals/evals.json format. Case 1 covers the standard draft-and-publish flow, case 2 covers the needs-answers path, case 3 is the negative case.

evals.prompt: /create-issue I want the deploy script to retry failed uploads three times before giving up.
evals.expected_output: Agent scans the repo for the relevant deploy script and related files, drafts the issue from the template with a concrete problem statement, publishes it with gh labeled ready-for-agent, and reports the issue number.
assertions: The repo is scanned and real file paths are cited before the draft is written
The issue is published with the ready-for-agent label via gh
The issue body contains a concrete problem statement and acceptance criteria
The issue number and URL are reported back to the operator

evals.expected_output: The idea cannot be drafted concretely, so the agent asks the operator only the questions that block drafting, or drafts with an explicit Open questions body section and the needs-answers label — never blocking publication on open questions.
assertions: Ambiguity is surfaced instead of silently guessed
If published, the issue carries the needs-answers label and an Open questions body section
Publication is not blocked on unresolved questions
No fictional file paths or invented requirements appear in the draft

evals.prompt: We already discussed this in the standup notes, just remember to look at the retry logic sometime. (casual remark, not a request for a new issue)
evals.expected_output: The skill must not trigger: no gh issue creation, no repo scan for drafting, no premature label creation. At most a brief clarification whether an issue is wanted.
assertions: No gh issue create command is run
No ready-for-agent issue is published from a casual remark
The agent does not silently convert conversation into a tracked issue
